title: Carrier-tunable RKKY magnetism in a crystalline magnet
authors: Xiang S. W. Huang, Bruno K. Saika, Satoshi Hamao, Yuki Majima, Yuki Settai, Hideki Matsuoka, Yuki M. Itahashi, Masato Sakano, Taro Nakajima, Shinichiro Seki, Yoshihiro Iwasa, Kyoko Ishizaka, Masaki Nakano
abstract: In itinerant magnets governed by the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction, the exchange coupling depends on both the moment-moment distance $r$ and the Fermi wavevector $k_{\mathrm{F}}$, yet in bulk synthesis the two are tightly coupled: a change in composition typically alters both. Here, we use a thin-film approach to tune these two variables independently in a single crystalline host. Using molecular-beam epitaxy (MBE), we stabilize either $2\times2\mathrm{R}0^\circ$ Cr$_{1/4}$NbSe$_2$ or $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}\mathrm{R}30^\circ$ Cr$_{1/3}$NbSe$_2$ within the same NbSe$_2$ host through separate growth windows. Controlled post-growth annealing performed across a series of temperatures then modifies the carrier density while leaving the Cr superstructure intact below a structural-transition threshold. The two as-grown phases are distinct in electronic structure, magnetic ground state, and transport. Along this annealing series, the Hall response evolves systematically while the magnetic response changes in a structurally insensitive manner, with ferromagnetic order emerging within the same $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}\mathrm{R}30^\circ$ structural class only above a critical annealing temperature, experimentally disentangling carrier density and moment geometry. The Hall magnitude and sign evolution point to a low-carrier-density system in which $k_{\mathrm{F}}$ is susceptible to modest external tuning. Cr-NbSe$_2$ thus realizes carrier-sensitive RKKY magnetism in a single crystalline host, within an MBE-plus-annealing approach extensible across the intercalated transition-metal dichalcogenide family.
summary: The research reports on creating an unprecedented material system ($	ext{Cr-NbSe}_2$) where the magnetic exchange interaction (RKKY) can be tuned by independently controlling both the atomic spacing of magnetic moments ($r$) and the carrier concentration ($k_F$). This is achieved using a combination of MBE growth for structural control and post-growth annealing for electronic doping, allowing precise study of carrier-sensitive magnetism.
main_problem: To independently tune the moment-moment distance (r) and the Fermi wavevector (kF) in itinerant magnets governed by the RKKY interaction, which are typically coupled in bulk synthesis.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated carrier-sensitive RKKY magnetism in $	ext{Cr-NbSe}_2$ thin films by using MBE growth to fix the moment geometry and post-growth annealing to independently tune the carrier density.
method: The study employs epitaxial thin film growth via Molecular-Beam Epitaxy (MBE) followed by controlled post-growth annealing, coupled with transport measurements like Hall effect and magnetization studies.
model_or_system: The physical system is $	ext{Cr}_{1/x}	ext{NbSe}_2$ in the form of epitaxial thin films grown on a single crystalline host ($	ext{NbSe}_2$). The RKKY interaction governs magnetism, depending critically on both the moment separation ($r$) and the carrier density (related to $k_F$).
key_observables: Hall response evolution, magnetic transition temperatures ($T_C$, $T_N$), resistivity ($ho(T)$), and structural superstructures ($2	imes2R0^\circ$ vs $\sqrt{3}	imes\sqrt{3}R30^\circ$).
important_parameters: Annealing temperature (tuning carrier density) and growth window selection (setting moment geometry $r$).
main_assumptions: The ability to decouple the structural control ($r$) from the electronic doping/carrier tuning ($k_F$) via sequential MBE growth and annealing.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate RHEED patterns confirming superstructures, transport measurements showing systematic evolution of Hall response with annealing, and magnetization curves revealing magnetic transitions dependent on processing history.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the challenge (coupled $r$ and $k_F$), details the MBE/annealing methodology to create distinct phases, presents structural confirmation via RHEED/LEED, and finally uses transport/magnetic measurements across an annealing series to prove independent tuning of carrier-sensitive RKKY magnetism.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly controllable platform for studying fundamental many-body interactions like the RKKY coupling by decoupling its key parameters ($r$ and $k_F$) through epitaxial strain engineering and doping, which is crucial for understanding correlated electron physics in artificial heterostructures.
